title: unanchored regex label matchers over-match via ClickHouse's substring match()
summary: PromQL and LogQL regex label matchers (=~ / !~) lowered a matcher's raw pattern text straight into ClickHouse's match(), which is a SUBSTRING search, while Prometheus's and Loki's own regex matcher semantics are always fully anchored. job=~"ap" wrongly matched job="api" and job="apiserver" in addition to job="ap"; the same substring-search lowering fed both heads' stream/label-matcher path (not LogQL's separate, already-anchored line-filter parser).
root_cause_subsystem: internal/chsql/builder.go:846 (anchoredRegexPattern), the single chplan.OpMatch/OpNotMatch SQL-emission site both internal/promql/lower.go's matcherToExpr/metricNamePredicateOn and internal/logql/lower.go's matchOp route a label matcher's pattern through; no anchoring existed anywhere upstream of it before the fix.
discovery_narrative: Found by direct, ad hoc empirical probing of the project's own chDB engine (match('0.1','1')=1, match('0.1','1|2.5')=1, both wrong under anchored semantics) while implementing the unrelated le-matcher restriction algebra for issue #1478, not by any automated verifier catching a live query. The issue body names this a 'neutralized-equals-missing' class: existing regex-matcher fixtures used patterns like .+/.* that could not exercise the anchoring boundary, so no compat-suite red had ever surfaced it.
mutation_class_rationale: The defect is precisely where the FULL-match/CONTAINS-match boundary is drawn: ClickHouse's match() tests containment, Prometheus/Loki's regex matcher tests full-string equality against the pattern. internal/chsql (the fix's home) is in gremlins' Phase 2 rollout, but the historical defect itself was an omitted ^(?:...)$ wrap — a call-omission no single gremlins operator (.gremlins.yaml's eleven arithmetic/conditional/bitwise/loop-control mutators) models, so this class label is this module's own taxonomy rather than a gremlins mutator ID.

contracts.locator_detail: up{job=~"ap"} against seeded job values ap/api/apiserver/web (-- seed --); -- expected_rows -- pins exactly the job="ap" row, so job="api"/job="apiserver" answering would fail this fixture's chDB roundtrip.

{service_name=~"auth"} (stream selector) and {service_name="auth-service"} | service_name=~"auth" (label filter) against a seeded service_name="auth-service" stream; "auth" is a strict prefix, so both queries must resolve to zero results on cerberus AND reference Loki.
